about: Edits that wmf-sbx-setup --claude-md applies to the CLAUDE.md sbx writes in the parent directory of the primary workspace. Each edit names a section by its exact heading line. A section runs to the next heading of the same or a higher level. 'contains' lists text that must be in the section, so a changed upstream section fails loudly. All edits apply, or none. See sbx/NOTES.md §95.

edits.heading: ## Git workspace mode
edits.text:
## Git workspace mode

This sandbox is in **neither** of sbx's two workspace modes. wmf-sbx made
a private git clone of each repo and mounted it over the host's path, so
the paths are the same as on the host, but your edits and commits are
**not** visible on the host. The engineer sees them only after they fetch
from this sandbox, so commit before you stop. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` gives
the details and the fetch command.

Do not use the `[ -d /run/sandbox/source ]` probe. It says "direct mode"
here, and that is wrong. The host's remote for this sandbox is named
`$SANDBOX_NAME` exactly, with no `sandbox-` prefix.

edits.heading: ## Git Authentication
edits.text:
## Git remotes and pushing

`origin` is Gerrit, not GitHub, and `local` is the engineer's own checkout
on the host. There is no pull-request flow here. Your work reaches the
engineer when you commit: they fetch it from this sandbox (see "End your
turn with a commit" in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`). Do not push to Gerrit or
anywhere else unless the engineer asks you to.

edits.heading: ### .NET Aspire: IPv6 loopback (`[::1]`) and the proxy
## Claude Code: Environment Persistence
edits.text:
## Claude Code: Environment Persistence

`CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is set to `/etc/sandbox-persistent.sh`, the file that
"Environment Persistence" above describes. Claude Code sources it before
each Bash tool call. The rules above apply: never add shell completion
scripts to it.
